findings: The stationary active position is the exponentially weighted history of fixed-speed orientation. Stationary angular Brownian motion is reversible, so its past has the same path distribution as the forward process used in the angular Feynman–Kac solver.

The forward tilted angular generator starts from the uniform orientation coefficient; its zero Fourier coefficient integrates over terminal orientation and gives the signed characteristic. Translational OU motion is independent and contributes exp(-diffusion*q²/(2*trap)).

The independent complex polynomial hierarchy decreases total position degree. Rotational invariance fixes the angle exponent q-p, and the recurrence preserves that exponent as either position degree decreases. The radial Bessel-series factor and scaling by speed/trap are correct.

The Gaussian propulsion approximation shares the exact free MSD and trapped variance but differs in stationary higher position cumulants. Complete microscopic fixed-speed orientation data determines these hidden signed Fourier measurements.
